title: 1966 AHSME Problem 11
statement: The sides of triangle \(BAC\) are in the ratio \(2:3:4.\) \(BD\) is the angle-bisector drawn to the shortest side \(AC,\) dividing it into segments \(AD\) and \(CD.\) If the length of \(AC\) is \(10,\) then the length of the longer segment of \(AC\) is:

solutions.text:
The sides adjacent to angle \(B\) are in ratio \(3:4.\) By the angle-bisector theorem, \(AD:DC=3:4.\) The longer of the two parts is therefore \[ \frac4{3+4}\cdot10=\frac{40}{7}=5\frac57. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Since \(AC\) is the shortest side, the adjacent sides are in ratio \(3:4\)
